keys.description: uvicorn bind port
app log level

the build this CONTAINER is running, stamped by whoever started it and reported verbatim by GET /api/version. Deliberately NOT derived from the source tree: the answer has to be true of the container, and a container knows nothing about the repo it was built from. The blue/green deploy sets it to the tag it is deploying (PRD decision 39); unset reads as "unknown", so an unstamped deployment simply never offers the terminal's reload bar
the runtime kernel's runtime.v1 surface the dispatcher spawns workers on (+ schedule.v1 for routines)
the opaque runtime.v1 profile the worker is spawned under (P11)
how the runtime's scheduler reaches THIS service's /invocations sink when a routine fires
where the dispatch's workspaces materialize inside the worker
workspace git ref the dispatch pins

the s3 workspace backend (WS-S3): where a worker reaches agent-api's store routes to hydrate its mounts and push its commits — an http(s) URL; unset or non-http derives the gateway's /agent/workspace-store from VEXA_MCP_URL. Ignored on the volume backend

where workspace repositories live: volume (the tree under VEXA_WORKSPACES_DIR is the truth) or s3 (an S3-compatible bucket is the single durable truth and VEXA_WORKSPACES_DIR a disposable cache; a write is acknowledged only once durable in the bucket; boot self-tests the bucket and fails loud)
s3 backend: the bucket's endpoint, a full http(s) URL (Linode: https://us-sea-1.linodeobjects.com; on-prem: the operator's)
s3 backend: the workspaces bucket — its own, never the recordings bucket
s3 backend: the key prefix every object is written under
s3 backend: the signing region; optional
s3 backend: path-style requests (https://host/bucket/key); false for virtual-hosted style
s3 backend: a PEM file of the private CA the endpoint's certificate is issued under
s3 backend: the access key id of a static key scoped to the workspaces bucket
s3 backend: the secret of that key

adopt a workspace's pre-0.13.4 policy records into the policy store. A workspace tree's policy/members.json, visibility.json, connections.json and invites are read ONCE, by the boot sweep (migrate_policy_store); when that sweep adopted everything, the store records it (.policy/_tree_adoption.json) and no read and no later boot reads a tree again, so leaving it unset is safe and needs no follow-up. A sweep that could not reach the store records nothing and the next boot retries. The interim .policy files (registry backend) and a closed room's participant rows are platform state and are still adopted on first read. 0/false/no/off adopts nothing at all, the boot sweep included: an unmigrated workspace then reads as having no members
s3 backend: the per-workspace Redis write lock's TTL (extended while a publish runs)
s3 backend: agent-api evicts least-recently-used workspaces (each a published generation, re-hydrated on next use) to keep its cache under this many bytes; set it below the emptyDir sizeLimit
s3 backend: a workspace used in the last this-many seconds is never evicted

keys.default: (unset — every mount's readers unknown: a marked session's change is held)
keys.description: who besides the person reads each mount of the dispatch — a JSON object {mount path: [readers] | null}, read by agent-api from the membership store (private_taint.mount_readers); null when that store could not be read. The worker's commit hold counts it, never the tree's policy/members.json mirror; each turn's signed stream entry carries a fresh copy (readers). Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface

keys.default: (unset — derived per dispatch: the private baseline only)
keys.description: the ordered THREE-TIER mount STACK the dispatch stamps into the worker spec — a JSON list [{slug,path,role,write,primary}], one entry per mount: _global (RO) + the active workspaces (RW) + _system (RW) (AMENDMENT 4 / WP-A1.1). Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface

keys.default: (unset — the in-store <VEXA_WORKSPACES_DIR>/_global, created empty at boot)
keys.description: host path / repo dir of the GLOBAL SYSTEM workspace (_global), first in EVERY worker stack — behaviour/skills/tools (AMENDMENT 4). Optional: unset means agent-api's own in-store _global, created empty if absent (founder ruling 2026-10-08: _global may be empty). A live mount: updating this one repo propagates to all agents next turn. A configured path that is missing or not a directory fails dispatch closed

RETIRED (founder ruling 2026-10-11) and IGNORED: it used to name user ids whose workers mounted _global read-write. The company layer is now written only by the deployment's ADMIN ACCOUNT, which identity decides (admin-api VEXA_ADMIN_ACCOUNT; control_plane/global_layer.is_admin_account). Read only so the boot can warn a deployment that still sets it that nobody it names writes _global any more. No deploy target sets it.
pin the _global mount to a ref (branch/tag/sha) for safe rollout of a global behaviour change; empty = mount HEAD (AMENDMENT 4, Q17)
the authenticated human principal's name the dispatch stamps for per-mount commit attribution (D4: git author = principal, committer = platform). Runtime-injected per dispatch
the authenticated human principal's email for per-mount commit attribution (D4). Runtime-injected per dispatch
the per-dispatch unit:<id>:out/:in streams the control plane relays (SSE) + the transcript tail

what a spawned agent worker connects to Redis as. `per-workload`: a Redis user of its own — its own unit's input stream, output stream and read cursor — defined at spawn and removed when it ends; the service connection never reaches it. `shared`: the service connection, for a Redis that cannot define users (some managed services); every agent worker can then read and write every other's keys, so it is safe only where every person on the instance trusts every other. The service's own Redis user needs ACL SETUSER/DELUSER for `per-workload`.
the per-subject workspace tree this control plane reads (WorkspaceReader) and seeds

Lane W: seconds a turn-commit waits on the per-shared-workspace write lock (cross-process flock serializing concurrent members' commits, shared/adapters.py) before raising WorkspaceBusyError — bounded so a wedged holder can never stall a workspace forever
the registry of workspace templates (one validated seed per subdir)
where the home caches the avatars and company icons it fetched (home_media); a cache, rebuilt on loss
explicit, already-resolved seed dir override (tests / special deploys)
which workspace template new subjects are seeded from (a subdir of VEXA_WORKSPACE_SEEDS_DIR). agent-api stamps it into every worker, which loads that template's skills and seeds from it

the model id every agent turn runs on — the chat turn and the write-back phase alike; the key Settings → Models writes and the dispatch stamps into every worker. Empty means the harness's own default, which exists only for the CLI harnesses: the openai-agent harness has no default host and no default model and refuses the turn with a named-key error rather than asking an endpoint for an empty model

agent harness stamped onto dispatched workspace turns: claude-code (default) | codex (the Codex app-server) | openai-agent (this repo's own loop over any OpenAI-compatible endpoint). The deployment FLOOR only — Settings → Models pins a harness per subject and the dispatch overlay wins. The openai-agent lane is configured by VEXA_LLM_BASE_URL / _API_KEY / _MODEL / _EXTRA_BODY, which the runtime forwards into the worker from its own environment; a subject's own Settings → Models endpoint replaces all four for that subject, because the dispatch stamps them and the runtime never overrides a stamped key
operator gate on workspace-pinned models (comma-separated)

keys.default: (empty — no catalog: every turn runs on VEXA_AGENT_MODEL / VEXA_RUNNER and each person's Settings → Models)
keys.description: the operator's model catalog (ADR-0043): one JSON object validated against core/agent/contracts/models.v1 Catalog — the providers this deployment reaches (each naming its adapter: openai_compatible, openrouter, anthropic) and the models people pick per chat in the terminal, each a real model named by its id at the provider. Refused WHOLE at boot, every problem named and no value quoted. Holds no credential: a provider's secret_ref (env:VEXA_MODEL_SECRET_<NAME>) names a variable in agent-api's environment, delivered by the deploy surface's secret store (compose .env, Helm models.catalogSecrets)

stamped by the dispatch, never set by a deploy surface: `subject` on a worker whose model route is the person's own Settings → Models endpoint. The claude-code harness then removes any stored credential from the CLI's config directory before the CLI starts, and refuses the turn when it cannot, so the only credential on that route is the person's own

keys.default: (empty — the deployment’s own gateway host(s) plus api.anthropic.com and openrouter.ai)
keys.description: operator allow-list for the base_url a SUBJECT may pin under Settings → Models (comma-separated host globs). A subject-chosen endpoint is an outbound destination picked by a non-operator and the worker carries a model credential to it, so anything unmatched is refused at dispatch with a friction record. Loopback/link-local/private addresses and single-label docker service names (redis, admin-api) need an EXACT literal entry — a wildcard never reaches the deployment’s own network
chat worker warm-serve window after its last turn (s) — a follow-up inside it lands on the warm worker
tool.v1 descriptors + MCP launch specs a unit's tools resolve against
how often the one-time move of old routines into flows retries until it completes, then stops (0 runs one pass at startup)
brokered, scoped identity the worker presents (ADR-0003)

the shared key agent-api signs each dispatch's identity token with (dev tier; k8s → SPIRE behind the same seam). It had a published default, `dev-dispatch-signing-key`; anyone holding that value can mint a token this key would sign, so the boot refuses it, the placeholders, and an unset key. Generated at install on every deploy surface: compose's mint-dev-env.sh, the Helm chart's Secret (kept by lookup), the Lite entrypoint (kept under $VEXA_LITE_STATE_DIR)
the gateway base URL for 'add bot from URL' (POST /bots) and the transcript relay's numeric→native resolve
API key this control plane presents to the gateway (mint one via admin-api / `make all`)

DOCKER-HOST path to a claude credentials JSON. agent-api does not use it itself — the RUNTIME bind-mounts it into every spawned worker at /root/.claude/.credentials.json for the claude CLI to read (a consumer subscription is never moved into the model proxy; see the runtime's config.v1) — but the agent plane's /health surfaces whether ANY model-credential path is configured, because that is where the operator looks when chat fails, and Settings → Models "Test" reads the mirrored file. PAIR IT WITH HOST_CLAUDE_DIR: the single-FILE mirror is inode-pinned and goes stale on the CLI's next token refresh

keys.default: (unset — only the legacy single-file mirror is available)
keys.description: DOCKER-HOST path of the claude config DIRECTORY (~/.claude), mirror-mounted READ-ONLY at /var/lib/vexa/host-claude. Settings → Models "Test" (control_plane.config_test) resolves .credentials.json inside it PER CALL. Same credential as HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS in the shape that survives a refresh: the CLI replaces the file via rename(2) (NEW inode) and a single-FILE bind stays pinned to the original inode, so this surface reported an already-refreshed token as expired for 32h (dogfood, 2026-08-31). Set it to the parent of HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS

Path to a codex subscription auth.json the runtime mounts into every spawned worker for Codex itself to read (a consumer subscription is never moved into the model proxy) — compose bind-mounts it; on k8s/helm the runtime mounts it from a Secret (RUNTIME_K8S_SECRET_MOUNTS) and this key is set on agent-api purely so the model-credential capability reads configured

the worker's Codex home: Codex's state, and the subscription auth.json the runtime mounts there. The runtime names it for every worker it spawns (runtime_kernel.workload_env.WORKER_CODEX_HOME) and the Codex CLI reads the same variable, so the mount and the read cannot disagree. No API key is ever placed there (H5/W1)
API-key credential for the claude-code harness. Read by agent-api alone, which seals it into the turn's model route for the model proxy (H5/W1); no worker ever holds it
bearer token for ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (a gateway such as OpenRouter, or Anthropic itself). Read by agent-api alone and sealed into the turn's model route; no worker ever holds it (H5/W1)

claude CLI subscription OAuth token (`claude setup-token`). agent-api stamps it into a worker only on the deployment's SUBSCRIPTION route, where the claude CLI reads it itself (a consumer credential is never moved into the model proxy); on every other route it is stamped empty
claude-CLI/gateway endpoint — an endpoint selector, not a credential alternative; dispatch stamps it (with the credential it pairs with) into every worker spec env

identity admin-api base URL over the internal tier (with INTERNAL_API_SECRET): the workspace registry (roster, visibility, connections, invites, closed rooms' members — agent-api adopts every file-store and in-tree policy into it at start while VEXA_POLICY_LEGACY_READ is on), the users.data.memberships[] index, orgs, presence, the admin check and the workspace principal a room's turn runs as. Empty = the file policy store under the workspaces root and an in-memory index, and a room's turn gets no toolbelt while VEXA_ROOM_WS_PRINCIPAL is on

meeting-api base URL — agent-api owner-scopes the live SSE feed (GET /api/meeting/stream) by hitting GET /meetings/{id} on it before opening the redis transcript stream (P0 cross-tenant leak fix, SSE sibling of the by-id ownership check). compose relies on the default service DNS name, helm sets it explicitly to the release-qualified Service DNS (unset it fails closed → 403 for the owner, #677), lite overrides to localhost

THE internal-tier shared secret — one name across every service (the compose/helm secret key). agent-api both PRESENTS it (Lane M: X-Internal-Secret on the admin-api membership-index edge) and BELIEVES it: `_internal_caller` compares this value, and gate 0 of the meeting room is by the code's own statement the trust boundary on who is in the room. Unset it used to mean `_internal_caller` simply returned False; the boot now refuses instead, because a half-configured internal tier is not a degrade an operator can see. Read through an alias so the deprecated VEXA_-prefixed spelling still works for one release (shared/config.py).

the runtime caller credential agent-api presents (`Authorization: Bearer`) on every runtime.v1 and schedule.v1 call — worker spawns, routine jobs, the admin panel's workload list. The runtime refuses any other caller; the same value is set on the runtime and on meeting-api, and never stamped into a worker. Unset, the boot refuses: every dispatch would be refused by the runtime

gateway-identity.v1 verification key: a file holding the gateway's Ed25519 PUBLIC key (SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM). agent-api rebuilds every x-user-* header from a verified signature and refuses (401) an identity that is neither signed nor carried by the internal tier, and forwards the verified token unchanged to the credential broker on every agent-role call. It verifies and cannot sign; a private key in this file refuses the boot, as does a missing file or any other key type. Generated at install with the gateway's signing key: compose's identity-keys one-shot, the Helm identity-keys ConfigMap, the Lite entrypoint

keys.default: (unset — DEPRECATED alias of INTERNAL_API_SECRET; read only when the canonical name is absent, and the boot logs a deprecation warning)
keys.description: DEPRECATED spelling of INTERNAL_API_SECRET. One secret had three names (INTERNAL_API_SECRET in compose/helm and in admin-api/gateway/meeting-api, VEXA_INTERNAL_API_SECRET here and in the terminal, VEXA_INTERNAL_SECRET in flows) and the drift is what let a placeholder survive on one spelling's refusal list and not the others (F95). No deploy surface sets it on agent-api any more; it is still READ so an operator mid-upgrade is warned rather than 401ed. Delete once the terminal reads the canonical name too.

keys.default: (unset — the post-meeting room resolves no participant and mounts ZERO desks)
keys.description: admin-api's ADMIN token, used for ONE question: resolve a meeting participant's email address to a subject for the post-meeting room (control_plane.meeting_room). The narrow door does not exist yet — agent-api's internal-secret tier on admin-api exposes no by-email lookup, and GET /admin/users/email/{email} sits behind this much broader credential (it can also create and patch users). Empty by DEFAULT and the room degrades to ZERO desks without it, never to matching a person by name. Delete this key once admin-api serves GET /internal/users/by-email/{email} returning only {id}: agent-api already prefers that route

keys.default: (unset — GitHub only; every unlisted host takes GitHub's bare-token form)
keys.description: the git providers besides the built-in GitHub (shared/git_provider.py): a JSON list of {name, kind: github|gitlab, baseUrl (https), label?, caBundle? (PEM of a private CA) | caFile?, apiUrl?} — or the earlier comma-separated <host>=github|gitlab|basic:<username>. Each provider decides how a token is presented on clone, pull, push and publish (gitlab: oauth2:<token>), where its API is (create a repository, nested GitLab groups included; check a token), the CA its TLS is checked against, and which saved token it receives (one per provider in the credential broker). A per-call token written <user>:<token> is used as written. Parsed at boot; a malformed entry is a boot refusal naming it

os.pathsep-separated list of directories a caller-supplied workspace repository may live under as a scheme-less local path (POST /api/workspace/swap|activate). Unset — the default and every hosted deployment — refuses local paths outright; a self-hosted deployment that legitimately clones from a disk mirror names its roots here. Values are resolved and proven contained before any filesystem access (control_plane/repo_ref.py)

Settings→Models Test button: the deployment-default STT backend URL probed by GET /api/transcription/test when no user/global override exists (the same env floor bot_spawn falls back to in meeting-api; rides in via env_file .env). Empty → the test reports 'no backend configured'
SECRET — the token paired with TRANSCRIPTION_SERVICE_URL for the on-demand /balance probe (Settings→Models Test). Never logged or echoed; only a pass/fail summary leaves the service

where a person's own terminal lives — the origin every scaffold link is built on (PRD §5.5). Deliberately the SAME variable name the flows lane already reads (core/flows/src/flows_steps/common.py UI_URL): one deployment fact, one name, because two spellings of a host is how a link ends up naming somewhere the person cannot reach. Unset, the mint route answers 503 rather than returning a url with no origin — a mint is what a step checks BEFORE it sends, and VEXA_UI_URL being set nowhere is exactly how every deeplink the rig ever minted pointed at a port nothing serves (PRD §3.3)

the MCP endpoint a spawned worker attaches as its `vexa` toolbelt: the gateway's /mcp, where the ONE assembled MCP server serves the meetings, agent and flows tools (ADR-0037). Every deploy surface points it at the in-network gateway

the symmetric HS256 key agent-api SIGNS each worker's per-dispatch delegation token with (shared.delegation); identity's /internal/validate verifies it with the same value, so the gateway authenticates the worker's tool calls as the person it acts for. Empty must mean ABSENT, never 'signed with nothing'. Generated at install on every deploy surface

where agent WORKERS reach the model proxy (control_plane.model_proxy, `python -m control_plane.model_proxy` on port 8102): every base-URL name a harness reads is stamped to <this>/llm, and the worker presents its per-turn token there instead of a provider key (H5/W1). Empty ⇒ no worker is given any model credential and every turn fails at its first model call — the key is never handed to the worker instead. compose http://model-proxy:8102 · helm the chart's model-proxy Service · Lite http://127.0.0.1:8102
keys.default: (empty — no worker is given a model credential)

keys.description: the key agent-api seals each turn's model route (endpoint, credential, models, output cap) with before it rests in Redis, and the model proxy opens it with — the same value on both. Empty on agent-api ⇒ no route is sealed and no worker gets a model credential; empty on the proxy ⇒ it refuses to start. Generated at install on every deploy surface (compose mint-dev-env.sh, the chart's Secret, Lite's entrypoint)
keys.default: (empty — no route is sealed; generated at install on every deploy surface)

keys.description: codex harness API-key credential for the OpenAI API. Read by agent-api alone and sealed into the turn's model route; the model proxy sends it (H5/W1). No worker ever holds it
codex harness API-key credential (an alternative name to OPENAI_API_KEY). Read by agent-api alone and sealed into the turn's model route (H5/W1). No worker ever holds it

keys.default: (empty — then the retired store's own generated key under the workspaces secrets root, if one is there)
keys.description: DEPRECATED — read only to move Git credentials an older build kept on agent-api's own volume (saved GitHub tokens, deploy-key private halves) into the credential broker, which is now their one store (ADR-0040). Nothing is sealed with it any more. Keep it set until the boot log no longer reports Git credentials waiting to move, then remove it

lifetime in seconds (at least 60) of a minted MCP delegation token. The token is revoked when its unit ends (control_plane/delegation_revocation.py); this is the bound when that never happens. The default covers a unit that runs one turn (900 s, the openai-agent harness's per-turn ceiling) and then its warm window. A unit still running when half of this has passed is handed a new token (control_plane/delegation_refresh.py), which its worker picks up before its next turn; the replaced token stays good until its own expiry, so a turn has half of this as headroom

D2 (0.13.4): mint a room turn's delegation token for the workspace's own numeric principal (identity's `principals`, asked over POST /internal/principals/workspace via VEXA_ADMIN_API_URL; token `principal_kind: workspace`, the speaker as `on_behalf_of`) instead of the owner's account. identity answers the owner as `bills_to`; identity unreachable or unconfigured means no toolbelt for the turn (fail closed). false: a room token is the owner's, narrowed by its ceiling, `shared` and the D3 shared-route table

ring limit (room_ring): how many times one caller may ring one person in any 10 minutes; a ring over it rings nobody, and call_person answers 429 ring_rate_limited with Retry-After before starting anything
ring limit (room_ring): how many rings one caller may send, to anyone, in any 10 minutes

D36 tuning line (S4): ring a DERIVED member of an open room's call only if they opened the room within this many days, so an org-wide open workspace does not ring everyone; a closed room's members are always rung

keys.default: (unset — derived per dispatch: minted by the dispatcher, never configured)
keys.description: the short-lived scoped delegation token the dispatcher stamps into the WORKER's env (subject + regime + workspace scope + exp + jti); the worker takes it out of its environment at boot and writes it, as an Authorization header, into an MCP attachment in a private directory outside every mount (shared/private_dir.py, 0600 for the harness's user). Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface

keys.default: (unset — derived per dispatch: the subject the dispatch acts for)
keys.description: the PERSON this dispatch acts for — the quota and credential-brokerage axis, and the subject the worker's timeline preamble is scoped to (PRD decision 31). Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface

flows' address — the domain this service HANDS FACTS TO (desk.unscaffolded, claim.proposed, workspace.invited — an invite for an address this instance does not know, which flows mails; Vexa-ai/vexa#1632 — and routine.paused, a scheduled routine the harness switched off after repeated identical refusals) and reads the worker's read-only timeline preamble from. Declared as the publish edge because that is what it is: agent-api needs no answer from flows — the publishes are bounded at 2s and swallowed (control_plane/publish.py) and an absent timeline degrades a turn rather than failing it, so unset is the no-flows PROFILE and not a degraded state. NO DEFAULT, and the class forbids one for the right reason: a fallback address to publish to, invented by us, in a deployment that deliberately runs no such domain

the READ-ONLY key that opens flows-api's GET /timeline and nothing else (flows_api._timeline_key). This is the one to set: VEXA_FLOWS_API_KEY is the OPERATOR key and would let every worker container submit and activate flows

flows-api's OPERATOR key, sent as X-Flows-Operator-Key on the same edge (renamed by #1486; flows reads the old spelling for one more release and this edge does not send it) — flows' POST /events is authenticated, so a publish target without its credential is a publish that always 401s — and since Vexa-ai/vexa#1632 one of those facts is an INVITE, so a 401 here is a mail a person was told had been sent, and the pair is what makes the edge real. Declared as part of the edge rather than beside it: unset alongside an unset url is the no-flows profile, unset with a url set is a deployment whose facts are being refused, and one declaration shows both. The read-only VEXA_FLOWS_TIMELINE_KEY opens GET /timeline and nothing else, so it cannot stand in here

how long a subject's rendered timeline block is reused across dispatches — fresh enough that a meeting that just ended is in the next turn, cheap enough that three messages in a row cost one round-trip
how long the worker waits for the timeline route before giving up on the block for this turn (a failure is cached like an answer)
how many past events the per-dispatch timeline block states (decision 31 §1: a handful of lines)
how many scheduled meetings the per-dispatch timeline block states

openai-agent harness: the deployment's OpenAI-compatible endpoint the turn's chat/completions run against. Unset, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL applies. A subject's own Settings → Models endpoint that passes VEXA_MODEL_BASE_URL_ALLOW replaces it for that subject: the dispatch stamps this key and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to the subject's endpoint, and the runtime never overrides a stamped key

openai-agent harness: the deployment's bearer token for VEXA_LLM_BASE_URL. Optional — a self-hosted vLLM behind the deployment's own network needs none. Unset, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN then ANTHROPIC_API_KEY apply. Read by agent-api alone and sealed into the turn's model route (H5/W1); never sent to a subject's own endpoint, where the route carries the subject's own key (empty when they set none)

openai-agent harness: a fallback model id, read only when no VEXA_AGENT_MODEL reaches the worker. The worker passes VEXA_AGENT_MODEL (what Settings → Models writes, under VEXA_MODEL_ALLOWLIST, and the dispatch stamps) into every turn, and it wins. Stamped empty when a subject's own endpoint applies, so this deployment value never names the model sent there

keys.default: (unset — on only when VEXA_LLM_BASE_URL is api.openai.com)
keys.description: openai-agent harness: whether a picture attached to a chat message is sent to the endpoint as an image (`on` | `off`). A self-hosted model that cannot read images refuses the whole request, so unset means on only for OpenAI's own API. Either way the agent is given the file's exact path in the text. claude-code and codex always send pictures natively

openai-agent harness: a JSON object merged into EVERY chat/completions request — the escape hatch for server-specific fields the OpenAI dialect cannot express. THE ONE DIAL WITH NO ANTHROPIC-DIALECT EQUIVALENT, and load-bearing: a self-hosted Qwen returns nothing parseable without {"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}, and a mis-stamped value fails SILENTLY (the turn runs with thinking on). A subject's own Settings → Models endpoint carries its own extra_body instead (stamped empty when they set none); the deployment's is never sent there

every harness: the output-token cap a model request asks for. claude-code receives it as CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS and openai-agent sends it as max_tokens; codex does not read it: Codex 0.146.0 has no setting for the model's output cap (its own max_output_tokens fields are per-tool exec budgets), so a Codex turn asks for Codex's default; empty keeps each harness's own default (the claude CLI asks for 32000, which a provider that prices the allowance up front refuses on a small balance with a 402)
openai-agent harness: stream the completion (SSE). 0/false/no sends one blocking request per step instead — for an endpoint whose SSE is unreliable

keys.default: (unset — WebSearch is NOT attached to the turn)
keys.description: openai-agent harness: the search endpoint the WebSearch built-in queries. THE OPERATOR SUPPLIES IT — no search engine ships with Vexa, and that is a licence decision as much as a deployment one (the obvious self-hosted metasearch is AGPL-3.0). Unset, WebSearch is simply not attached and the turn's tool list says so; WebFetch needs no backend and is always attached

openai-agent harness: which wire format VEXA_SEARCH_URL speaks — `searxng` (JSON output, `?format=json`, which the operator must enable) or `brave` (Brave Search API, needs VEXA_SEARCH_API_KEY). An unknown value is a failed tool result naming the dialects this build speaks, never a silent no-op

keys.default: (unset — fine for a dialect that needs no credential)
keys.description: openai-agent harness: the credential for VEXA_SEARCH_URL. `brave` sends it as X-Subscription-Token; `searxng` needs none

openai-agent harness: ceiling on tool calls, the FALLBACK FOR EVERY KIND of turn. A turn that reaches it stops, says so in the bubble and offers a Continue act. Per-kind overrides: VEXA_AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS_CHAT / _JOB / _ROOM / _FLOW
openai-agent harness: tool-call ceiling for a CHAT turn — a sentence and its follow-through. Falls back to VEXA_AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS

openai-agent harness: tool-call ceiling for a background JOB (Create/Extend), PER WINDOW — reaching it is a checkpoint, not a death. Falls back to VEXA_AGENT_JOB_MAX_TOOL_CALLS, then to VEXA_AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS, and is never below a turn's
openai-agent harness: tool-call ceiling for a post-meeting ROOM run — one pass over a finished meeting, which is measurably longer than a sentence. Falls back to VEXA_AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS
openai-agent harness: tool-call ceiling for one FLOW step. Falls back to VEXA_AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS
openai-agent harness: hard per-turn wall-clock ceiling in seconds, reported the same way as the tool-call budget

openai-agent harness: estimated-token budget on a request, a deployment-wide value. With a model catalog the dispatch stamps the chosen model's own window less room for its answer, which wins; an entry with no window leaves this value in force. Over it, the history is compacted quietly (oldest tool results first, never a person's message or the latest exchange)

keys.default: (unset — always stamped per dispatch: build_unit_env's own workload id)
keys.description: the stable per-dispatch workload id (`dispatch.dispatch_id`), set on EVERY dispatch unconditionally. #1510: worker/friction.py's `fallback_session()` reads it as the friction carrier's session ref when no chat session exists at all (a scheduled/event/transcription dispatch never sets VEXA_CHAT_SESSION) — the flows carrier refuses a report with no session, so a stable id here is the honest fallback rather than a made-up string. Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface

keys.default: (unset — stamped per dispatch with the dispatching request's trace; the worker mints one when absent)
keys.description: the logevent.v1 trace the dispatch was made under (Vexa-ai/vexa#1783). The worker runs its entrypoint turn under it and sends it as X-Trace-Id on its MCP attachment, so the turn's tool calls join the request that started it; later turns take theirs from the signed stream entry. Correlation only, never a credential. Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface

keys.default: (unset — present only on a post-meeting room dispatch)
keys.description: the meeting this dispatch is the POST-MEETING RUN for, stamped when a room was authorised and absent on every other dispatch. Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface. The worker reads it for the three things decision 22 says a room run must not do: no entity write-back and no desk-README refresh against the subject's own desk (both committed there, moved HEAD, and failed the meeting on process_meeting's own detector — F103), and no bot verbs in the MCP allow-set for a meeting that is over (F104). A POSITIVE signal rather than an inference from the mount set, because a room whose other attendees have no desks yet resolves to zero room mounts — the small-team case — so the mount shape answers 'not a room run' on a run that is one

keys.default: (unset — present only when the chat has chosen one; unset means the person's own desk)
keys.description: the chat's TARGET WORKSPACE (Vexa-ai/vexa#1611) — the one slug this conversation's writes go to, while every other mount in the stack is there to read. Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface. The worker reads it to MARK that mount in its own `## Your mounted workspaces` block, so a file operation with no better instruction has a path rather than a guess; agent-api says the same fact in the person's vocabulary (`target workspace: <name> — writes go here unless asked otherwise`) and points the turn's cwd and the delegation token's default `slug` at the same place. A POSITIVE signal rather than an inference from which mount is `primary`, because `primary` also answers for a room run's group desk and for an ordinary subject's own baseline. Founder, 2026-09-06: “it creates files in the wrong workspace, we need so that the thing knew the workspace of writing, if it's specified”

keys.default: (unset when the listing cannot be read — the worker then gives no workspace hint)
keys.description: the person's workspaces as [{slug,name}], hidden ones left out — runtime-injected per dispatch (UI decision 6b). The worker compares what a request names with the chat's target and, when they differ, tells the model to call propose_write_target before writing. Names only, never a credential.
the dispatch's ``start`` object as JSON (the entrypoint ask or the session ref). Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface

keys.default: (unset in agent-api — stamped per dispatch; a worker without one runs no input-stream entry)

keys.default: (unset in agent-api — the runtime injects the worker's connection per dispatch)

openai-agent harness: the most fresh windows a chat turn may continue into (0-50). Validated by agent-api at boot and stamped into every worker.

keys.default: (empty — no restriction: every signed person is served the agent tier)
keys.description: who agent-api serves the agent tier to (control_plane/agent_admission.py, read per request after the identity door): empty or unset = everyone (the default); `*` = everyone; otherwise a comma list of user ids, email addresses and `@domain` entries, case-insensitive. A signed person not on it is refused 403 `agent_tier_not_enabled`; health, the internal tier and a worker acting for an admitted person are not refused

keys.default: (empty — the release default: every switchable feature off)
keys.description: the install's switched-on features (control_plane/features.py): empty = the release default, every unproven feature off; `all` = every one on (a dev stack); a comma list switches on just those; `all,-name` takes one back. `features:` in _global/POLICIES.md overlays it per company for the features that are not install-scope. A switched-off route refuses 403 `feature_disabled` and its tools leave the served manifest

`1`/`true`/`on` refuses every agent turn before dispatch (chat, routine, sensor, event agent) with a typed refusal, whatever the spend ledger says (control_plane/llm_budget.py). The spend caps themselves are `_global/POLICIES.md` keys (llm_budget_*).

The market price table the spend ledger prices a call's tokens at when the call reports no cost (control_plane/model_prices.py): OpenRouter's public models list (no key), read at most once a day and cached in redis. `off` never reads the network (air-gapped installs); the price snapshot bundled with the release prices every call instead.

connections.description: Connections: the agent can request, list and use a person's connected accounts and services through the credential broker, without ever receiving a credential
connections.when_unconfigured: every /api/connections* route answers 503 'Connections are not configured on this deployment', and so does /api/onboarding/research for `start` and `next`, which reach the broker; its `status` and `ack` answer from the research already stored. person_resolution.description: one Person, many addresses (PRD 0.13.4 D35): agent-api asks crm-api which Person each account resolves to by its verified address, so the @ picker lists a Person once and a grant to the Person reaches every account linked to it
person_resolution.when_unconfigured: every account is a Person of one: the picker lists accounts as before and a grant reaches only the account picked
